jobs.title: Research Scientist
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.

About the Role

New and novel approaches are needed to realize all of our product goals. As a Machine Learning Scientist at Sesame, you are a research-oriented person with experience in NLP, Speech, and/or Computer Vision with a focus on deep learning. You are up to date on recent papers and approaches and you have the creativity and the intuition to come up with new solutions based on the application at hand.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to the development of our ML models across multiple modalities.

  • Work across the ML stack, including model architectures, data curation, model evaluation, training & inference infrastructure, research, and experimentation.

  • Pick promising approaches from the literature to bet on, and create new approaches where necessary to achieve our unique goals.

Required Qualifications:

  • Experience working independently in high-ambiguity environments.

  • Published papers in NLP, Speech, or Computer Vision involving large-scale deep learning.

  • Familiar with the state of the art in AI.

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in CS or related field.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Masters/PhD desired.

  • Experience working with products.

  • Experience in a startup environment.

Sesame is committed to a workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered. We welcome all qualified applicants, embracing diversity in race, gender, identity, orientation, ability, and more. We provide reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.

Responsibilities:

  • Turbocharge our serving layer, consisting of a variety of LLM, speech, and vision models.

  • Partner with ML infrastructure and training engineers to build a fast, cost-effective, accurate, and reliable serving layer to power a new consumer product category.

  • Modify and extend LLM serving frameworks like VLLM and SGLang to take advantage of the latest techniques in high-performance model serving.

  • Work with the training team to identify opportunities to produce faster models without sacrificing quality.

  • Use techniques like in-flight batching, caching, and custom kernels to speed up inference.

  • Find ways to reduce model initialization times without sacrificing quality.

Required Qualifications:

  • Expert in some differentiable array computing framework, preferably PyTorch.

  • Expert in optimizing machine learning models for serving reliably at high throughput, with low latency.

  • Significant systems programming experience; ex. Experience working on high-performance server systems—you’d be just as comfortable with the internals of VLLM as you would with a complex PyTorch codebase.

  • Significant performance engineering experience; ex. Bottleneck analysis in high-scale server systems or profiling low-level systems code.

  • Always up to date on the latest techniques for model serving optimization.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with high-performance LLM serving; ex. experience with VLLM, SGlang deployment, and internals.

  • Experience with a public cloud platform such as GCP, AWS, or Azure.

  • Experience deploying and scaling inference workloads in the cloud using Kubernetes, Ray, etc.

  • You like to ship and have a track record of leading complex multi-month projects without assistance.

  • You’re excited to learn new things and work in a multitude of roles.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.

About the Role

Sesame AI is building deeply integrated hardware + AI products and is opening a fabrication shop and prototype line in Bellevue, WA. We're looking for a Fabrication Shop Manager to build it, staff it, and run it.

You'll develop and prove out the manufacturing processes our products depend on and build them into a repeatable proto line. You'll work closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and industrial design engineering to turn concepts into production-representative builds that inform product and DFM decisions.

The ideal candidate has run a machine shop or pilot line, is fluent in CNC and joining processes for plastics and metals, and cares as much about how a part gets made as how it looks when it's done.

Responsibilities

Shop Design & Build

  • Work with the team to design a functional & flexible space to meet current & future proto needs

  • Drive detailed layout equipment selection and procurement, utilities, safety, and IT

  • Manage build & equipment install and commissioning

Manufacturing Process Development

  • Develop, characterize, and document processes for CNC machining (multi-axis, metal and plastic)

We're looking for an Eyewear Designer who is passionate about creating luxury fashion eyewear that blends refined aesthetics, advanced materials, and thoughtful user experience. This role requires a strong sense of style, a deep understanding of frame construction, and the ability to translate trends, CMF direction, and brand DNA into distinctive, production-ready designs.

You bring a trained eye for proportion, fit, and fashion relevance, and the technical rigor to move seamlessly from concept through manufacturing. You will shape collections that express traditional eyewear craftsmanship and contemporary design excellence at the frontier of what personal computing can look and feel like.

Concept Development

  • Generate innovative eyewear design and CMF concepts that align with our brand's aesthetic, fashion direction, and user needs; contributing to and helping define our design language.

Design Execution

  • Conduct fit studies, wear testing, and ergonomic evaluations to ensure frames are comfortable, balanced, and suitable for extended daily use.

  • Iterate on designs based on user insights, testing feedback, and internal reviews to optimize comfort, usability, and visual appeal.

  • Maintain a strong focus on nose bridge fit, temple comfort, weight distribution, and overall human factors.

Collaboration and Communication

  • Work closely with engineering, manufacturing partners, and material suppliers to ensure design feasibility and production accuracy.

  • Communicate design rationale, specifications, and CMF decisions clearly to internal teams and external vendors.

  • Participate in design and prototype reviews, offering constructive feedback to elevate design quality and execution.

Industry Trends and Innovation

  • Stay informed on global fashion trends, eyewear silhouettes, color directions, and emerging materials.

  • Bring new fabrication techniques and fashion influences into concept development with intention and editorial point of view.

Required Qualifications:

  • Strong portfolio showcasing both creative and technical design skills, with an emphasis on eyewear, accessories, or wearable products.

Sesame is building a wearable AI hardware device that brings our voice companion into the physical world. We're standing up our hardware quality function from the ground up, and we're looking for our first dedicated Hardware Test Automation Engineer to build the automation backbone for the program. You'll design and own an automated test rig, a rack of devices wired into our CI/CD pipeline that, on every firmware change, builds, flashes, runs the test suite, and generates reports automatically. You'll establish nightly stability runs, weekly stress runs, and long-duration audio sessions, and you'll build the live performance and stress dashboard that becomes the team's shared source of truth for quality. Your metrics will gate releases and back the performance story we tell investors and customers.

This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role at the firmware/wireless/hardware boundary, on a small team that moves fast. You'll partner closely with the firmware team and our hands-on platform tester, and you'll have visibility and authority across both the firmware and the testbed so the two are built to cooperate.

Initial focus (first ~60 days):

  • Stand up an automated test framework driven from a programmable Bluetooth central (Android, iOS, or a Pi-based rig, whatever fits), firmware-first then integration-first; even if early runs are short, get the foundation in place before it scales.

  • Establish nightly (sanity/stability) and weekly (stress) automated runs, with extended weekend runs for long-duration audio sessions (e.g., 5-hour and 18-hour using synthetic data).

  • Begin a live performance/stress dashboard: A2DP/throughput, BT link duration, BT latency, battery life, firmware crash counts, and regression flags.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and own an automated hardware test rig integrated with CI/CD (build → flash → run → report) for the device.

  • Implement throughput/bandwidth, connectivity stress tests (e.g., iPerf, A2DP/AVRCP), including sustained-throughput, connection-stability/range testing, and simulated degraded-connectivity scenarios.

  • Build API-level tests (easier to automate than full end-to-end iOS flows) covering throughput, sustained load, and crash detection.

  • Run long-duration audio session testing (multi-hour, synthetic data) and battery/thermal performance characterization (including full discharge cycling).

  • Build and maintain a live performance & stress dashboard with defined safety thresholds and target ("high-achieving") benchmarks; automatically flag regressions.

  • Develop diagnostic tooling and support automated bug triage for hardware/firmware issues.

  • Provide daily automation summaries and updates; support ad hoc/cherry-picked test runs when the team needs targeted coverage.

  • Partner with firmware (and the QA coordinator) to define what is automated vs. manual, API vs. integrated, and which platform drives the rig.

Required Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience building hardware/embedded test automation and integrating it into CI/CD (automated flashing, execution, and reporting).

  • Solid wireless/networking fundamentals: Bluetooth audio (A2DP/AVRCP), BLE, and throughput testing (e.g., iPerf). You understand what to test, not just how to automate.

  • Strong scripting/programming (e.g., Python) and the ability to build harnesses and dashboards from scratch.

  • Experience defining test plans, metrics, and pass/fail thresholds from real data.

  • Comfortable operating in an early-stage, prototype-hardware environment with limited units and evolving specs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience owning an automation testbed for a shipping consumer hardware product (wearables, audio devices, smart cameras, IoT).

  • Performance instrumentation experience: latency, sustained throughput, IPC/cycle count, and thread- and core-level tracing on embedded/multi-core platforms.

  • Familiarity with Qualcomm chipsets and tooling (e.g., DSP framework, PyDebug) and the realities of vendor bug turnaround.

  • Experience automating from a programmable Bluetooth central: Android, iOS, a Pi-based rig, or similar; bonus for breadth across more than one.

  • Battery and thermal test methodology.

  • Experience with sensor/IMU testing and creative physical test setups for connectivity/range.

About the Role

Sesame is an interface company. We're building the most human interface for intelligence. Our personal agents, like Maya, hold natural conversations and make the devices they run on more useful. We're looking for someone to lead this team.

A word on how we think about management here. You're not there to track progress or supervise employees. You're an engineering leader: someone who guides a team of engineers to incredible outcomes, chosen to lead because of consistent displays of great judgment. People leadership is a crucial part of that, and you treat it as essential to what makes you great, not the boring work someone has to do.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive the team's outcomes. Lead product engineering to ship products people love. You're accountable for results, not just execution.

  • Stay hands-on. You're continuously prototyping, fixing bugs, de-risking projects, and improving quality of life for the team. You plug into the work and show the team how to get more out of the tools available to engineers today.

  • Be responsible for the quality bar for products serving millions of people: reliability, security, performance, and polish. Your team owns its software end-to-end, including deployment, reliability, and production operations.

  • Grow the engineers on your team. Give clear, actionable feedback, create opportunities for people to do the best work of their careers, and hold a high bar for performance.

  • Build a talented, diverse engineering team by attracting and hiring exceptional engineers.

  • Partner closely with product and design. We have skilled product designers; you don't need to be the primary product visionary, but you need real judgment about what makes a product people love.

  • Set technical direction for the product stack and make the architectural calls that keep it simple, reliable, and fast to build on.

Required Qualifications:

  • You've managed engineers and led teams through complex projects to outcomes you're proud of. We care about the track record, not the title.

  • 10+ years as a software engineer, including 5+ years managing a team of 5+ engineers.

  • You're a full-stack product engineer with real depth in scalable web infrastructure. You've built products on distributed systems serving millions of people and understand the reliability engineering that takes.

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great.

  • You're a software engineer at heart. You'll sit on the software engineering team, and you care as much about secure, reliable, well-crafted software as you do about delightful products.

  • Consumer hardware product experience, building the software side of a physical product.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.

About the Role

Sesame is integrating a complex sensing and computing system into a compact wearable that has to be light, comfortable and attractive, and available in many styles and colors. The Product Design TPM owns the program plan for the mechanical side of that product: enclosures and cosmetic parts, materials and finishes, mechanisms, packaging and accessories. You will carry hundreds of mechanical parts through design release, tooling, validation and factory builds, working with our Product Design, Industrial Design, Manufacturing and Operations teams and with our contract manufacturers and tooling and materials suppliers.

The ideal candidate has a mechanical or product design engineering background, has run part release and tooling for a consumer product through EVT, DVT and PVT, and knows how to keep design change under control when the schedule is tight and the design is still moving. You are comfortable telling a designer or an executive what a change will cost in weeks and dollars, and then building the plan that makes it happen.

We are a small team working on very ambitious projects. In a fast-paced startup, everyone must be comfortable, collaborative, decisive, and able to achieve results with limited supervision.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the Product Design program schedule from concept through EVT, DVT and PVT, including part release, tooling kickoff, first-shots, validation and phase exit criteria.

  • Run the PD release and change-control process: every part has a release date, an owner and a status in our PLM tool.

  • Program-manage styles, colors and materials: cosmetic material qualification, color development, SKU rollout planning.

  • Coordinate design validation and reliability testing for mechanical parts, and own closure of design-review action items.

  • Manage tooling, materials, cosmetic-part and packaging suppliers: quotes, POs, sample requests, tooling timelines and delivery schedules.

  • Plan mechanical materials and build matrices for prototype builds, and lead mechanical build readiness across factory sites.

  • Run failure analysis triage for mechanical and cosmetic issues: every issue has an owner, a due date and a path to closure.

  • Maintain the Product Design section of the program's master issues list and weekly status, aligned with area leads.

  • Travel to contract manufacturer and supplier sites for builds, tooling reviews and validation as needed.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • BS in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years of experience in hardware program management or mechanical/product design engineering of consumer electronics, with at least 2 years managing programs.

  • Hands-on experience releasing mechanical parts and taking them through tooling and prototype builds (EVT/DVT/PVT or equivalent).

  • Working knowledge of high-volume manufacturing processes (injection molding, machining, stamping, cosmetic finishing) and tolerance, DFM and validation practices.

  • Direct experience managing tooling, materials or fabrication suppliers, including quotes, POs, samples and schedules.

  • Experience running change control and part release in a PLM tool.

  • Strong written communication; able to run a program with clear plans, decision logs and status updates.

  • Ability to travel internationally, up to 25%.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with wearables or other products with heavy industrial design and cosmetic constraints.

  • Experience with premium cosmetic materials and finishes and their supply chains.

  • Experience managing many SKUs, colors or configurations through a single program.

  • Experience with packaging or accessories programs.

Join our team to craft a unique take on smart wearable devices with incredibly compact audio capabilities. We're looking for an experienced Audio System Engineer to define, tune, evaluate, and ship high-quality speech reproduction systems and spatialized audio capture solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Own aspects of shipping consumer electronic products with market-leading audio performance, independently or with the support of the Audio Lead depending on experience level.

  • Create the transfer function from product-level requirement documents to audio system and transducer requirements to ensure product success.

  • Design, analyze, and refine real-time audio capture and render systems.

  • Research and implement advanced technologies to optimize audio system integration.

  • Continuously learn and explore new technologies, setting benchmarks for user experiences.

  • Collaborate on system architecture, including algorithms and tools, and oversee implementation.

  • Evaluate third-party audio technologies and keep abreast of industry developments.

  • Understand the trade-offs in various DSP and ML approaches and platforms for embedded solutions.

  • Work with the cross-functional team to innovate on audio solutions.

  • Factory testing and build support throughout the product development cycle.

Required Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in audio hardware development, with at least one shipped consumer electronics product.

  • Experience in designing, tuning, and testing microphone arrays and real-time audio capture.

  • Track record in developing audio solutions encompassing acoustics, transducers, digital interfaces, audio ICs, and DSPs.

  • Hands-on experience with audio testing systems (e.g., SoundCheck, Audio Precision, HATS testing).

  • Background in DSP techniques (e.g., FIR/IIR filter design, beamforming, echo cancellation).

  • Effective independent operation and teamwork in a dynamic, cross-functional setting.

  • Experience with acoustic simulation software, e.g., COMSOL.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Acoustics, or similar.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in audio hardware development.

  • Proficiency in a high-level programming language (e.g., MATLAB, Python).

  • Familiarity with human perception of sound.

  • Experience with psychoacoustic metrics and evaluation of speech quality and intelligibility.

  • Familiarity with audio rendering techniques and speaker technologies.

  • Experience in acoustics and consumer audio EE architecture.

  • Familiarity with audio algorithm development, ML techniques, and/or neural network implementations.

  • M.Sc. or Ph.D. in EE, Computer Science, Acoustics, or related disciplines.
